text: Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1222, 271 CR 528, 530; and American Guarantee & Liab. Ins. Co. v. Vista Med. Supply (ND CA 1988) 699 F.Supp. 787, 793 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:378] A claim that the insured locked certain employees in the store at night against their will (i.e., false imprisonment) is potentially covered under a “personal injury liability” policy. [See North American Bldg. Maint., Inc. v. Fireman's Fund Ins. Co. (2006) 137 CA4th 627, 638, 40 CR3d 468, 476—“the false imprisonment allegation … comes within 5 the insuring agreement”] (3) [3:379] Ins.C. § 533 (“wilful acts”) exclusion: There is no express “intentional injury” exclusion for “personal injury liability” (as there is for bodily injury and property damage; see ¶ 3:311). But Ins.C. § 533 is read into every insurance contract and bars coverage for harm caused by the “wilful acts” injury of another (see ¶ 3:105 ff.).
